gao-gaoreports-gao-08-297r: Written in 2007 as a letter to Congress, this GAO report takes on the switch from old-style TV to digital. It fields hard questions about the coupon plan that helped homes buy signal boxes, and about the task force meant to steer the change. With the shutoff date near, the report warns that weak plans could leave viewers staring at dead screens.
gao-gaoreports-gao-08-267r: The 17th in a series Congress ordered, this 2007 GAO report tracks a 1998 law that gave many Haitians a path to green cards. It tallies how many cases were done, how many sat in line, and how much work was left. The report keeps the pressure on the immigration agency to finish a job promised nearly a decade before.
gao-gaoreports-gao-08-137r: This 2007 Government Accountability Office correspondence analyzes how a proposed change to Ryan White Care Act funding would affect urban areas. The act funds HIV/AIDS care for the uninsured, and Congress was considering a new formula. GAO's analysis shows which cities would gain and which would lose — hard numbers for a debate where funding shifts could disrupt care for thousands of patients.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-47r: GAO wrote Congress in 2007 on a gray-area drug question: were new pills truly tested on the old folks who'd swallow most of them? The letter reviews the FDA's push — and its gaps — in getting seniors into drug trials. The point is plain: prove the pill works for grandma, not just for the young and hale.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-1197r: Two agencies, two rulebooks, one pile of bomb-grade material — GAO's 2007 letter exposes the mismatch. The Energy Department and the atom regulators guarded weapons-usable stocks under different standards. The findings ask the obvious, uneasy question: is the nation's nuclear lock only as strong as its weaker key?
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-1037r: Downwinders and uranium miners sickened by the bomb tests got their due through this program — and GAO's 2007 letter checks its pulse. The status report tallies claims paid and work left for radiation victims. The findings keep faith with a Cold War promise: the nation would not forget those it irradiated.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-1157r: After the hearing came the homework — GAO's 2007 letter answers Congress's follow-ups on Homeland Security's tangled tech merger. The responses fill gaps the testimony left open. The findings keep the department's computer consolidation under the microscope, one pointed question at a time.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-787r: The military's shot clinics got a checkup in 2007 — GAO's letter reviews the vaccine healthcare center network for the troops. The findings assess the system guarding service members against germs and bioterror. The letter's premise: healthy troops start with smart shots.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-767r: Pentagon travel money got a line-item look in 2007 — GAO's letter reviews the department's reporting on trip spending under the clean-payments law. The findings check the receipts against the rules. The letter's premise: even warriors' expense reports deserve daylight and a second look.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-757r: The pension insurer's lawyers needed clearer marching orders in 2007 — GAO's letter says the legal advice was tangled and inconsistent. The findings demand one clear voice for the agency. The letter's fix: end the confusion before it costs retirees real money.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-667r: Disabled veterans' charity books got the audit treatment in 2007 — GAO's letter reviews the DAV's financial statements for the year. The findings give the formal audit opinion for the record. The letter proves that even the most honored causes get the auditor's careful once-over.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-437r: Federal workers' daycare needs got counted in 2007 — GAO's letter sizes up the dependent-care survey results for the federal workforce. The findings turn answers into solid estimates. The letter's quiet value: policy for parents built on facts, not on hunches.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-317r: Military families with special needs got a GAO check in 2007 — the letter reviews the medical, family, and school services for exceptional members. The findings inventory the support in detail. The letter's heart: the toughest duty is the one the family carries.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-347r: The bomb-sniffer tests were missing in 2007, and GAO's letter says the detection office had not gathered most of the labs' radiation-detector results. The findings flag the data gap. The letter warns that untested detectors are just expensive decorations.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-367r: The Air Force's tanker wanted to haul cargo too in 2007, and GAO's letter examines the decision to add passenger and freight capacity to the refueler. The findings probe the requirement. The letter asks whether the flying gas station needed to be a flying truck.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-327r: The Air Force sergeants' books got audited in 2007, and GAO's letter reviews the association's financial statements for the year. The findings give the formal opinion. The letter shows the NCOs' group faces the same ledger check. The stripes got their audit.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-297r: Yucca Mountain's email scandal got a price tag in 2007, and GAO's letter estimates the cost of answering the quality-doubting messages. The findings do the accounting. The letter shows even the nuclear dump's inbox had a bill attached. The questions cost real money.
